facts.label: Passado e past progressive
facts.sub: Use was/were + -ing para a ação em andamento e o passado simples para a ação curta: I was making dough when the owner came in.

facts.label: Ação longa
facts.sub: Para uma ação em andamento no passado, use was/were + -ing: I was making dough. Use was com I, he, she e it, e were com you, we e they.

facts.label: Ação curta
facts.sub: Para a ação que interrompe, use o passado simples: The owner came in. Aqui o verbo muda: come vira came, drop vira dropped.

paragraphs: It is early morning in a small bakery in Seattle. The oven is warm and the shop smells of bread. Sara wears a white apron. Her friend Felix comes in for a coffee. He knows it was her first day. He wants to hear the story.
“Hi, Sara! How was your first day at the bakery?” says Felix. “It was great! I was making dough when the owner came in.” says Sara. “What did she do?” says Felix.

pages.what: Was soa “uóz” e were soa “uêr”. Em was baking, o -ing é fraco.
pages.tip: Compare was e were: a vogal muda.

solo: Modele, peça repetição, depois uso livre.
group: Foco: was e were. Diga was como “uóz”, curto.
Coro, depois um a um; ouça sem corrigir tudo.
extra90: Cada aluno grava um áudio de 10 segundos e compara com o modelo.

pages.title: Encontre a frase natural

opts: I made dough when she came.
I was baking when she arrived.
I was baking when she was arriving.
items.why: After when, use the past simple for the short action.

pages.instruction: Escolha a forma que resolve a situação; explique o erro comum.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Escolha a frase mais natural. → I was making dough.
Escolha a frase mais natural. → I was baking when she arrived.
Escolha a frase mais natural. → She was watching me.
Escolha a frase mais natural. → They were baking.
